 A-League controversy sparks questions as pundit identifies worrying Wanderers trend: ‘I’m still not convinced’
 Western Sydney Wanderers had a goal disallowed in their draw against Macarthur. Image source: Paramount+ 
 Sacha Pisani 
 October 31, 2026 
 share 
 Facebook 
 X 
 WhatsApp 
 LinkedIn 
 1 
 Western Sydney Wanderers were left frustrated by a controversial offside decision in their goalless draw against Macarthur FC, with Paramount+ pundit and former A-League star Erik Paartalu leading the questions over the disallowed goal.
 Wanderers recruit German Ferreyra thought he had given Western Sydney a ninth-minute lead in Saturday night’s Derby of the West, only for his effort to be ruled out following a lengthy VAR review at Campbelltown Stadium.
 Ferreyra was deemed to be in an offside position, sparking an angry reaction from Wanderers head coach Ufuk Talay as unbeaten Western Sydney were denied back-to-back wins.

 The decision sparked debate among the Paramount+ panel, who struggled to identify a clear offside from the available camera angles.
 “The VAR must have had a better angle than what we’ve been given,” Paartalu said.
 “This is the offside camera. The point of contact, I can’t see a foot. I can’t see a foot that’s in front of the defender there. How is that conclusive?
 “Now, when they go and draw the line, what we see on TV, I’m still not convinced.
 “Yes, the foot from Ferreyra looks a little bit longer, but are we sure that the defender’s foot is in a position alongside him or before it?
 “So, for me, it’s a really unlucky one.”
 The frustration was shared by fellow pundit and A-League great Alex Brosque, who added: “I’m with Erik.
 “It’s hard to see amongst all those bodies how you could possibly give an offside.”
 Paramount+ co-commentator Andy Harper also questioned the decision as the teams returned for the second half.
 “I think the goal that was rubbed out probably should have stood,” Harper said. “After factual review, I couldn’t see any clear facts in that one.”
 The controversy continued after full-time, with Brosque and Paartalu acknowledging the VAR lines indicated an offside but questioning whether the available footage made the decision sufficiently clear.
 “When you see the lines that are drawn, yes, there’s a clear distance between the blue line and the red line,” Brosque said.
 “When you look at this angle and the other camera angles that we have, it is hard to see that it is as obvious as one might suggest.
 “It’s near impossible for us to make that determination.”
 But the disallowed goal was not the only talking point to emerge from the stalemate among the Paramount+ panel, particularly for Paartalu.
 Despite remaining unbeaten through their opening three matches under new boss Talay, Western Sydney – who finished bottom of the table for the first time in their A-League Men history last season, have now failed to score in two of them.
 Their 5-2 demolition of reigning champions Auckland FC was sandwiched between goalless draws against Sydney FC and Macarthur, raising questions about the consistency of their attack.
 “Two nil-nils, though, either side of a 5-2 result against Auckland,” A-League champion Paartalu said. “That’s what I’d be worried about if I was a Wanderers fan or a Wanderers coach.
 “You can score five one week. We’ve actually been shut out. We had no answers on either side.
 “I hate to be negative about it, but it is a great improvement and step forward.”
 Brosque, though, responded by saying: “At the moment, yes, they probably haven’t been breaking [teams down] in two of them, but at least they’re finding ways to not lose games.
 “So I think that’s a positive for them. They’re on the right track.”
